messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER DUTY — SEV2: increased inference errors and p99 token latency from az1a (us-east-1a). Alert group: inference-paths. Paging @alice oncall.

alice: ack — I'm on it, joining now. Pulling logs and dashboard.

ben: seeing packet loss on ENI telemetry for az1a starting ~2026-03-17T09:12Z. rx_err/tx_err spikes, grpc stream drops. kvcache miss rate jumped ~8x.

alice: thanks @ben. Can you paste the ENI error metric query?

ben: `sum(rate(eni_transmit_errors[1m])) by (az)` -> az1a is #1. Also `kvcache.misses_total` shows a big spike at 09:12Z. Correlation looks strong.

chandra: any signs of autoscaler flapping or pod restarts?

ben: pod restarts are low. It's not app OOMs. Network-level packets being dropped before gRPC handshake completes for some upstream instances.

infra-runbooks: Runbook ref: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/az-egress-kv-churn (follow section "egress-pktloss -> reroute"). Recommendation: temporarily steer traffic off az1a, enable model-variant fallback and increase client-side retries.

alice: immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert new inference sessions away from az1a via smart-router policy (steer_percent=75% to eu-west-1, keep 25% for telemetry) 2) increase client retries to 3 with backoff 50ms 3) enable kvcache priming on standby pool.

chandra: I'll execute router change. Applying policy now: `redwood-router apply --policy route_policy=latency_prefer --override az1a=25`

chandra: applied. Confirming traffic shift in router metrics. New-requests to az1a down ~72% within 30s.

ben: verifying downstream: ENI error rate trending down, kvcache miss storm abating where traffic shifted. p99 latency for affected models dropping back toward baseline.

support-eng: customer impact snapshot: ~40 customers saw elevated error rates between 09:12Z-09:40Z. Top impacted tenant (Acme Corp) had ~18% request errors, now down to 1.2%. Customers with dedicated capacity unaffected.

alice: drafting status update for ops-status: "Investigating network packet loss in az1a impacting hosted inference. Traffic shifted to eu-west-1; error rates improving. Working with infra to root cause and with cloud provider if needed."

ben: collecting packet captures from a sample host and saving to s3: `s3://inference-incident/3980012345/pcap-host-7.pcap` for post-mortem.

chandra: also enabling temporary model-fallback to quantized variant (lower memory path) for high-throughput routes to reduce KVCACHE pressure: `deploy --model-route inference-main --variant quantized-fallback --pct 50`

alice: note: we'll keep ~25% traffic on az1a for telemetry to validate recovery. If error rate < 0.5% for 30m we can start gradual reshard back.

infra-runbooks: recommend opening cloud support ticket (INC/CloudNet) — suspected NIC driver or host egress queue saturation. Include ENI metrics and pcap.

chandra: creating ticket with AWS support and attaching graphs + pcap. Ticket: AWS-INC-98765.

support-eng: preparing customer comms: short note to affected customers describing mitigation and ETA for root-cause. Tagging accounts with temporary rate-limits if needed.

alice: handing off to @chandra for next 2 hours of mitigation and cloud-eng escalation. I'm available if needed. :thumbsup:

chandra: taking over incident. Monitoring dashboards and the router policy. Will update in 15m or on any change.

ben: preliminary hypothesis for postmortem: host-level NIC tx ring exhaustion + kvcache storm causing retransmit cascades. Will gather histograms and instance-level counters.

chandra: update 09:58Z — AWS responded: they see egress queue tail drops on a subset of instances in az1a, working on host remediation. Continuing traffic steering until hosts stabilized.

alice: thanks team. I'll schedule the incident write-up and severity review once we have AWS confirmation.

support-eng: closing customer-facing alert draft for review by @alice.

chandra: 10:30Z — error rates steady at baseline with current routing. Keeping incident open until AWS provides root-cause.

pagerduty-bot: Incident handoff logged: incident_id=3980012345, current_owner=chandra, severity=sev2, status=mitigated but open.

chandra: noted. We'll move to postmortem when AWS confirms host remediation.
